data.body:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED — it is NOT merge commits.

This ticket was filed saying plain `git log` skips MERGE commits, so a deletion reaching HEAD
via a merge was invisible. That is wrong. Measured on the live store against f130's lost EDIT
(a440f6d5-6aa1-4669-9908-5fb955ad6a53):

  git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                        -> 0 hits
  git log --diff-filter=D --full-history -- <tid>/         -> 0 hits
  git log --diff-filter=D -m -- <tid>/                     -> 0 hits
  git log --diff-filter=D --diff-merges=first-parent -- .. -> 0 hits
  git log --all --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                  -> 0 hits
  git log --all --diff-filter=D          (no pathspec)     -> 0 hits
  git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/*<uuid>*                -> 1 hit

Every merge-diff flag and --all changes nothing; ONLY narrowing the pathspec from the
DIRECTORY to the FILE (or a per-uuid glob) finds it. So it is a pathspec-SCOPE effect under
git's path history simplification, not merge-diff display and not reachability. The fix the
original ACs implied (add a diff-merges mode) would have shipped without fixing anything.

FIX PUSHED: keep the cheap directory pass, add a per-uuid glob fallback bounded to the uuids
the snapshot still cites as absent (the glob walks full history per uuid and is much slower).
The restore cluster also moves to a new fsck_restore leaf because fsck_repair was at its
module-size cap.
